chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I said to him, 'The nakedness of the believer is prohibited upon the believer?' He said: 'Yes'. I said, 'You mean his lower part?' He said: 'It is not where you are going with it. But rather it is the broadcasting of his secrets'.

key_terms.عَوْرَة: Nakedness or private parts; metaphorically, secrets or vulnerabilities

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of a believer's 'nakedness' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Imam distinguishes between the physical 'awrah' and the spiritual 'awrah,' defining the latter as the concealment of a believer's secrets (idha'at sirrihi). This interpretation shifts the focus from bodily modesty to the ethical imperative of guarding personal privacy, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding social conduct and the prohibition of backbiting (ghibah).

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘The nakedness of the Momin is Prohibited upon the Momin?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Youasws mean his lower part?’ Heasws said: ‘It is not where you are going with it. But rather it is the broadcasting of his secrets’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad from al- Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once I asked him (abu ‘Abd Allah) (a.s.) ‘Is it unlawful to publicize the secrets and privacy of a believer before another believer?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is unlawful.’ I then asked, ‘Do you thereby (privacy) mean his two lower organs (anus and genitals)?’ The Imam said, ‘It is not what you thought it is. It is to publicize his secrets and private matters.’”
